members.name: connectAppControl
members.summary: Connects to one explicit running native window for background document inspection, viewport capture and targeted DOM actions.
members.availability: Node local IPC on Windows, Linux and macOS; the current window adapter is Windows WebView2, with other native adapters unavailable
members.protocol: arcane/1 app.control.status, app.control.inspect, app.control.capture and app.control.act over the existing framed local connection. The window host selects native.launchContext.appControl.endpoint and preserves its existing Core child, origin, profile and lifetime.
members.normalization: Returns endpoint, closed, status(options), inspect(parameters={},options), capture(parameters={},options), act(parameters,options), and close(). Parameters pass unchanged; per-operation options preserve Core signal/timeout behavior. Status reports actual app/window/document readiness. Inspect returns complete selected top-level light-DOM HTML/text and live control state with DOM-derived role/name hints; frames and open shadow hosts are descriptors only. Capture returns mimeType image/png, complete base64 data, documentGeneration and URL for the rendered viewport. Act requires documentGeneration and one CSS selector with click, exact-string fill, exact-value select or absolute-offset scroll. The native document marker prevents queued actions crossing replacement; cancellation before dispatch prevents execution while dispatched work is observed through completion without retry or reversal. close() cancels only this connection, never the application or Core. No launch, automatic reconnect, desktop activation, global input or public arbitrary evaluator. See native-app-control.md for complete result fields, CLI and platform scope.

members.name: createExecutionDeviceCatalog
members.summary: Owns lazy physical-device discovery and saved device-ID resolution independently of models and inference.
members.availability: Node; Windows discovery is implemented, while other platforms return an unavailable inventory without changing existing AI behavior
members.normalization: Returns async devices({refresh=false,signal}={}), async resolveTarget({executionTarget=null,refresh=false,signal}={}) and dispose(). Construction performs no discovery I/O; calls share cached/coalesced discovery and refresh explicitly requests a new observation. Complete records and issues distinguish ready, partial and unavailable discovery. A saved deviceId resolves as matched, unavailable or unsupported; null returns automatic/engine-default-required without discovery, and a non-null target without a nonempty string deviceId throws TypeError. Physical presence never proves engine support or actual execution. Request cancellation rejects AbortError/ARCANE_CANCELLED and the last departing caller stops the query; retained dispose() joins owned discovery shutdown, and constructor-signal abort disposes the catalog. The direct caller owns disposal; no polling, model loading, preference writes or silent target substitution. See execution-devices.md for all record fields and reasons.

members.name: createNativeDecisionModel
members.summary: Explicit native Laya FP32/FP16 or Julia FP32 option scoring through an existing ONNX owner and a tokenizer Worker.
members.availability: Node on Windows/Linux/macOS with selected ONNX Runtime and model files; Android needs host adaptation
members.protocol: Shared browser/native decision encoding with native named tensor results. Factory and each load accept family/model/revision/dtype; omission or undefined retains the selected value. Laya FP32 defaults remain. Laya FP16 selects onnx/model_fp16.onnx and onnx/model_fp16.onnx_data; Julia FP32 selects model.onnx and model.onnx.data, with its own tokenizer files. Complete new-family selection and matching files are caller-owned. All model fields participate in activation equality; top-level metadata stays attributable to the retiring activation while pendingActivation records its requested successor. Decoder preserves raw probabilities, every original row and every actual output without inventing Julia action logits.
members.normalization: Returns load/evaluate/classify/current/status/subscribe/unload/dispose; preserves complete separate state/question/options/type and original rows, raw scores and every graph output. load({family,model,revision,dtype,assetProjectionId,resourcePaths,executionTarget,signal}) retains omitted or undefined family, model, revision, dtype, source, mapping and target fields from the latest selection, initially the factory configuration. A supplied ready projection takes precedence over configured paths and upstream settings; the existing modelAssets owner retains it directly without upstream preparation or fetching. resourcePaths maps model, tokenizer and tokenizerConfig to exact projection member.path values; complete companion files remain at their original relative paths. Missing projections or mapped members report their actual failure. assetProjectionId:null returns to configured paths or existing upstream preparation when no paths were configured. Separately, executionTarget:null requests automatic resolution, while {deviceId} forwards the saved physical selection to the existing ONNX owner. With no target selection, GPU preference still attempts advertised providers then CPU and explicit session providers retain precedence. Equal family, model, revision, dtype, source, complete mapping and target selections share activation; a changed selection cancels the earlier request and joins its actual ONNX/tokenizer cleanup before replacement. Incoming projection use is retained before retiring the previous activation; caller preparation ownership is independent, and native files remain retained through actual ONNX and tokenizer Worker exit. Unload ends native use; loading again after all ownership is released requires a fresh projection. pendingActivation reports the requested replacement and projected source/mapping separately; current().execution remains the complete ONNX load record, with requested/resolved/configured/observed target diagnostics in current().execution.execution. Configuration alone does not prove physical execution. Cancellation retires the shared activation. No preference writes, chat history or duplicate inference engine.

Factory, direct load and decisions.load accept family/model/revision/dtype with the direct model's exact variant, omission and replacement semantics. The service persists across explicit model changes; top-level activation metadata and pendingActivation distinguish the retiring and requested selections.
members.normalization: Registration starts no model or tokenizer. Explicit load obtains dependency-ready same-process owners and reacquires getONNXRuntime after recovery. Factory configuration accepts family, model, revision, dtype, assetProjectionId, resourcePaths and executionTarget; direct load({family,model,revision,dtype,assetProjectionId,resourcePaths,executionTarget,signal}) and Core decisions.load({family,model,revision,dtype,assetProjectionId,resourcePaths,executionTarget}) preserve omitted/undefined selections, with the Core request signal forwarded separately. resourcePaths maps model, tokenizer and tokenizerConfig to exact ready projection member.path values; complete companion members retain their relative paths. Supplied projections take precedence over configured paths/upstream settings, are retained through the existing model-assets owner, and never invoke upstream preparation or fetching; unavailable projections or mapped members fail directly. assetProjectionId:null returns to configured paths or existing upstream preparation, independently of executionTarget:null requesting automatic device selection. Equal family, model, revision, dtype, source, complete mapping and target selections coalesce; changed selections cancel pending work and join the prior model's disposal before replacement. Incoming retained ownership protects projection files while the previous activation retires; caller preparation ownership remains independent, and native use retains files through actual ONNX/tokenizer exit. pendingActivation includes a projected source/mapping separately from the full activation execution record and its nested execution diagnostics. Native load/evaluate/classify/current/subscribe/unload/dispose preserve complete results; RPC uses the existing tensor codec. Unload has accepted service lifetime; host shutdown cancels request-lifetime load/evaluation.

Requests cancelled while awaiting attachment are never submitted afterward. Subscriptions survive restoration; retired renderer promises abort while accepted service-lifetime work continues. Existing transport behavior is unchanged when omitted; see core-client.md for the native ownership and acknowledgement contract

Forwards optional webKitDocumentLifecycle:false by default; when selected, __arcaneWebKitDocumentCurrent(activation) probes the executing realm and __arcaneReceive(json,activation)/__arcaneTransportFailed(error,activation) reject delivery to retired or different activations before changing installation ownership

members.name: createCoreRuntime

Lookup is readiness, not a lifetime lease; new lookups reject during shutdown. Preserves complete results/errors, cancels request-lifetime work and drains accepted service work; runtime.replay publishes current dispatcher/service state without restart and preserves reentrant lifecycle publication order. Missing dispatch retains METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED with exact method/namespace and core-namespace-unavailable or core-method-unavailable; named services, registered methods and built-in namespaces establish presence.
